Subject: Internal: initial findings on token double-counting (incident 2026-04-26)

Internal note (sending in thread for transparency):

Summary: During the 2026-04-26 incident at ~03:12 UTC we observed a race condition in the request fanout logic that caused certain streaming requests to be re-queued and processed twice by the token accounting layer for a small subset of sessions. The runtime issued two increment events for the same logical tokens because the request acknowledgement path retried incorrectly when the KV cache reconnect completed.

Scope: ~0.6% of total tokens processed that hour across affected customers; for Vanguard Apps this resulted in ~109k tokens duplicated on two invoices (INV-2026-04-17, INV-2026-04-24) amounting to $4,280.

Work completed: identified faulty retry branch, pushed guard to dedupe accounting events, added logging around ack sequence IDs, and queued a follow-up change to make KV reconnect suppress retries.

Attached audit: billing_audit_20260427.csv — mapping of affected session IDs, timestamps, and duplicate token counts.

Next steps (ops & billing): Stephanie to calculate credit and generate credit note; Finance to confirm whether reissued invoices are preferred. Engineering will provide a one-page postmortem for your records.

Soojin Lee
Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: billing_audit_20260427.csv (CSV, 23KB)]

Hi Sara / Tom — following up with the remediation and next steps.

What happened (brief): during our 2026-04-26 incident a retry path caused a small set of streaming requests to be processed twice by the billing counter, resulting in duplicated token counts for a subset of sessions. Engineering has implemented a dedupe guard and additional ack-sequence logging to prevent recurrence.

What we did for Vanguard Apps:
- Applied a $4,280 credit to your account (see attached credit_note_VG-38.pdf).
- Issued corrected invoice lines for INV-2026-04-17 and INV-2026-04-24; your billing portal shows the adjustment and the net payable is now zero for those lines.
- Uploaded an engineering postmortem: redwood_postmortem_20260426.pdf.

Timing: the credit is visible in your Redwood billing account immediately and should reflect in your next payment cycle. If you require a refunded payment rather than a credit, please confirm and our finance team will initiate it and provide an ETA.

Attachments: credit_note_VG-38.pdf, redwood_postmortem_20260426.pdf
